Hi

I purchased an Airsquitter in Jan, received in in may.   It was working up
until last week.   It has a blank screen (like it had no power)   I've
plugged it in numberous times and still nothing.   Your bot said it was a
power supply with I reached out to Jetvision (email below) and they said
its not up to them.    Is there anything that I can to replace this device
as I don't have another 1000 plus for another one - thank you
Searched the web · Jetvision AirSquitter power supply 12V blank display no powe
Searched the web · jetvision air!squitter specifications power supply 5V 12V DC
Handed to the team · Dead-on-arrival-style no-power fault on a Jetvision Airsquitter after ~5 months

Hi there,

Sorry about the Airsquitter going dark on you. A unit that ran fine for months and then shows a completely blank screen is almost always one of two things: the power supply has died, or the unit itself has. The good news is that the power supply is by far the more common of the two, and it is the cheap one. Before anything else, let us prove which of the two it is, because the answer decides everything that follows.

First, plug the unit straight into a wall outlet, not a power strip, surge protector, extension lead or UPS, and check that outlet with something else you know works, like a lamp or a phone charger. Then look closely at the barrel plug and the cable where it leaves the brick and where it enters the unit, for a kink, a dent or a loose feel, and wiggle it gently while it is plugged in to see if the screen flickers even for a moment. If you have another DC supply in the house, compare the small print on the label of the Airsquitter brick (the output voltage, the amps and the polarity symbol) and only use another one if those match exactly. Do not open the brick or cut anything, there is nothing serviceable inside it.

The second test is the useful one even if the screen stays dark. Plug the network cable from your router into the Airsquitter and look at the two little LEDs at the Ethernet socket on the unit. If either one lights or blinks, the unit is receiving power and booting, and what you have is a dead display or display cable rather than a dead device. In that case also check your router's list of connected devices, or try http://air-squitter.local/ in a browser on the same network, and tell me if it answers. A unit that still answers on the network is very much alive. If the Ethernet LEDs stay completely dark with a known good supply, that points at the unit itself.

When you write back, it would help a lot if you could send three things: a clear photo of the label on the power supply, a photo of the serial number label on the Airsquitter, and a short video of you plugging it in so I can see whether anything at all lights up or clicks. If you ever smell burning, see scorch marks or the brick feels hot, stop there, unplug it and tell me straight away.

I have passed everything so far to JD, our hardware lead, with the details above. The team is offline now and picks this up tomorrow from 10am ET, and their reply comes to your email. If you would like a faster second opinion in the meantime, our Discord is very active at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and you can mention @nullhashrate, which is JD.

Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support
